findings.title: R4 modifier names inconsistent with R3 state-value syntax
findings.why_it_matters: R3 defines six mutually exclusive `data-tile-state` values (empty, correct, wrong, reject, pickup, ejecting). R4 introduces modifier attributes (`data-shaking`, `data-speaking`, `data-drag-over`) as separate boolean attributes. However, the evidence shows R4 using `data-shaking="true"` syntax while R3 uses attribute-value pairs. This creates ambiguity: does R4 mean boolean presence/absence (`[data-shaking]` selector), or attribute-value pairs (`[data-shaking="true"]`)? AE4 clarifies it as attribute-value, but AE3 and AE4 both show `data-shaking="true"` only when explicitly listed. An implementer might assume modifiers are CSS attribute presence checks, not parsed value checks, leading to CSS selector mismatches.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify R4 by adding explicit CSS selector form: 'Modifier attributes are present (boolean) on the element; CSS targets them via [data-shaking], [data-speaking], [data-drag-over] selectors.' OR revise to match R3's value-pair pattern: 'data-tile-modifiers="shaking speaking"` (space-separated). Then audit all evidence (AE3, AE4) to match chosen pattern.
evidence: R3: 'data-tile-state attribute with one of six mutually exclusive values: empty, correct, wrong, reject, pickup, ejecting'
R4: 'Orthogonal modifier attributes compose with primary state: data-shaking="true" (shake animation window), data-speaking="true" (TTS active), data-drag-over="true" (slot is hover target).'

AE4: 'when a tile is shaking (either bank-reject or slot-wrong-shake), the element has both data-tile-state="wrong" (or "reject") AND data-shaking="true". CSS rules targeting [data-shaking] apply the shared shake motion'

findings.title: R5 and R6 scope boundary unclear — slot-wrong-shake vs. bank-reject state routing
findings.why_it_matters: R5 states 'Shake animation and wrong paint are shared between bank-reject and slot-wrong-shake via the data-shaking modifier.' R6 states 'Bank-reject has its own appearance token namespace (--skin-tile-reject-*) separate from slot-wrong (--skin-tile-wrong-*). Classic defaults reject values to the same as wrong values.' This creates ambiguity: does R5 mean both bank-reject AND slot-wrong-shake set data-shaking="true" (shared visual trigger), OR does R5 describe only the slot-wrong-shake motion path?
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite R5 to be explicit: 'Bank-reject and slot-wrong-shake trigger the same data-shaking="true" modifier, applying identical shake animation. They differ in appearance tokens: bank-reject uses --skin-tile-reject-* tokens while slot-wrong uses --skin-tile-wrong-* tokens.'

findings.title: @property initial-value cannot contain var() references
findings.why_it_matters: R1 states tokens are registered via CSS @property with Classic skin values as initial-value. The CSS @property spec requires initial-value to be computationally independent — var() references are forbidden. Classic skin tokens overwhelmingly use var() references (e.g., 'var(--bs-primary)', 'rgb(from var(--primary) r g b / 0.1)'). Of 63 tokens in classic-skin.ts, the majority reference other custom properties. The plan's core inheritance mechanism cannot work as stated.
evidence: R1: 'Every skin token is registered via CSS @property with Classic skin values as initial-value.'
classic-skin.ts tokens use var() references: '--skin-tile-bg': 'var(--bs-primary)', '--skin-correct-bg': 'rgb(from var(--primary) r g b / 0.1)'
CSS @property spec: initial-value must be computationally independent — var() not permitted
